original_question: On a circle, black particles arrive according to a Poisson stream of rate lambda and remain there, while white particles arrive according to an independent Poisson stream of rate 1 and immediately disappear after, if possible, deleting the nearest black particle within distance epsilon of their arrival location. Is this model stable whenever lambda < 1, independently of the circle length and of epsilon?
target_in_paper: Section 3.2, "Stability of a model with two streams: stream of customers and stream of servers" (within Section 3, "Greedy service mechanism"), page 4.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core open problem very closely: two independent Poisson streams of black and white particles with rates lambda and 1; black particles remain unless deleted; a white particle deletes the nearest black particle within distance epsilon of its arrival point if one exists; and the conjectured stability condition is lambda < 1, uniformly over the circle length and epsilon. That is essentially the same problem stated in Section 3.2.
missing_details: The arrivals are not just temporal Poisson streams; they are Poisson rains on a continuous circle, so each arrival location is implicitly uniform on the circle.
The circle should be understood as having an arbitrary fixed positive length L, and epsilon should be an arbitrary fixed positive parameter.
The relevant distance and epsilon-neighbourhood are with respect to the circle metric.
The white particle chooses among black particles present at its arrival instant and deletes the nearest one in its epsilon-neighbourhood.

To make the question stand-alone, the stochastic object whose stability is being asked about should be named explicitly: the evolving black-particle configuration process (equivalently, the associated continuous-state-space queueing model).
The paper does not specify a tie-breaking rule for equally near black particles; on a continuous circle such ties have probability 0, so this is usually left implicit.

The paper frames this as a continuous-state-space model with a greedy/local rule, which helps distinguish it from the easier finite-state or state-independent variants mentioned immediately afterward.
refined_question: Fix a circle of arbitrary length L > 0 and a parameter epsilon > 0. Black particles arrive on the circle as a Poisson rain of rate lambda, with arrival locations uniform on the circle, and each black particle stays until deleted. Independently, white particles arrive as a Poisson rain of rate 1, with uniform arrival locations; each white particle immediately disappears, but at its arrival epoch it inspects the epsilon-neighbourhood of its arrival point (for the circle metric) and, if that neighbourhood contains any black particles, deletes the black particle nearest to it. Is the resulting continuous-state-space greedy system stable, for every lambda < 1, independently of the circle length L and of epsilon?
justification: This is the exact open problem stated in Section 3.2: the paper describes a circle with two independent Poisson rains of black and white particles of rates lambda and 1, respectively; black particles stop on the circle; white particles immediately disappear after deleting the nearest black particle in their epsilon-neighbourhood if one is present; and the paper says that the natural conjecture is that stability should follow from lambda < 1, independently of the circle length and epsilon. The surrounding Section 3 context identifies this as one of two continuous-state-space models whose difficulty comes from a greedy local rule. Your draft is therefore very close, but it leaves implicit the spatial-uniform Poisson-rain interpretation, the fixed arbitrary parameters L and epsilon, the circle metric, and the intended stability object/process, all of which help make the question fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper.
